CAST-1.title: Replay stamped a new receive time

CAST-2.title: An error answer that still committed

CAST-29.title: `@clickhouse/client` 1.23 replaces a per-query `Authorization` header with its own Basic header, so HyperDX's server-side queries (alerts, API, MCP) would reach the adapter with no token

CAST-50.title: A consumer checkpoint PUT got no answer; the read-back showed the checkpoint unchanged, so the worker kept its old version (17), but the store applied the write later (next = 21). GC acts on the stored checkpoint and deleted slots 17–19; the worker's scan then waited at a "gap" at 17 forever: the lane stalled for good and nothing after it was ingested

CAST-52.title: The query service's grants are a cluster set × a namespace set, not pairs: a principal granted `devtools/dev-payments` and `prod-eu-1/search` can also read `prod-eu-1/dev-payments` and `devtools/search` (`query/internal/auth/principal.go`)

H-1.title: Acknowledged telemetry is in no store and cannot be recovered

H-2.title: A result is presented as complete while it is missing or duplicating data

H-3.title: Telemetry is attributed to the wrong entity, or to none

H-4.title: An alert condition holds but no page reaches on-call, or a page fires for a condition that does not hold

H-5.title: People act on a stale or wrong view without knowing it (snapshot, source or mode confusion)

H-6.title: An unauthorized party can read or write telemetry, the catalog or control objects

H-7.title: A pipeline component uses resources beyond its budget

H-E1.title: Telemetry is committed under a tenant its sender is not entitled to write, or attributed to a person who did not send it

H-E2.title: A party that is not an authenticated member of the organisation, on the organisation's terms (device compliance, the right client), can write telemetry

H-E3.title: Device telemetry is readable beyond its owner's scope: in the device buffer (stolen or shared laptop), in transit, or at query time through a grant that over-reaches

H-E9.title: Sign-in friction makes the tool unusable (prompts, blocking calls on the tool's path)

L-1.title: An incident is missed, misdiagnosed or prolonged because operators lacked correct telemetry

L-3.title: Telemetry shown to people or alerts is wrong: duplicated, missing, stale or on the wrong entity

L-4.title: Sensitive data is disclosed (secrets or personal data in logs, one team's data to another)

L-5.title: Telemetry or the catalog is tampered with, hiding or forging activity

L-6.title: The pipeline harms production or budget: node pressure, full disks, runaway central or S3 cost

L-E1.title: The telemetry harms the developer's own work: the tool blocks, slows, or prompts for sign-in repeatedly, and people disable it (which in turn is L-1 for the teams relying on it)

LS-2.title: ClickHouse answered a timeout, but the insert committed up to 29 s later; the consumer's process model said "failed"

LS-3.title: A writer that never learned its write succeeded retried into a slot GC had already deleted, below the checkpoint

LS-4.title: A worker paused past its lease; its clock said it still held the lane

LS-7.title: A lane was lagging; the alert window closed on partial data and read as "no errors"

R-S4.title: Silences and pinned snapshots have an owner and an expiry, shown at handoff

R-S7.title: Writes are scoped by cluster prefix and role; edge keys cannot delete; the aggregator rejects mismatched clusters. Scheme (proposed, not built): cluster-first keys; publishers and entity controllers may only create under their own cluster's prefix, keyed on a cluster principal tag in the session credentials; only consumer roles can write or delete control objects. Recorded in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) D18

R-S9.title: The query service and rewrite proxy build SQL only from a parsed tree, with per-user limits

SC-1.title: Telemetry must not be acknowledged until it is durable, and must be ingested exactly once

SC-2.title: Every result must state its source and the time it is complete through; incomplete windows must be marked

SC-6.title: Every write path must be authenticated and authorized, and reads must be scoped by role

SEC-1.title: A compromised pod or node forges telemetry or entity records for other workloads

SEC-2.title: A stolen edge key overwrites or deletes lane objects

SEC-3.title: An attacker writes a lease or checkpoint to stall or skip lanes

SEC-5.title: A crafted query exhausts central or the lake readers

SEC-6.title: An insider silences alerts or edits rules to hide activity

SEC-7.title: Log injection makes the UI or proxy run unintended SQL
